summary: The first memo in the new FYI (For Your Information) sub-series of RFCs. It introduces the series and specifies no standard. It is historic and was replaced by RFC 6360.

plainLanguage.summary: A new set of friendly guide-books was starting. This is the introduction that explains what they are for.

where do i find fyi notes
subtitle: Introducing the FYI (For Your Information) notes as a new RFC subseries.

tldr.problem: The RFC series is a mix of technical standards and information documents, making it hard to find guides, answers, and background material separate from normative specifications.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1150 establishes a new FYI (For Your Information) subseries as a part of RFCs. FYIs cover historical context, operational questions, beginner guides, and other informational topics without specifying standards.
tldr.outcome: FYIs use the same proven RFC distribution system but serve a different purpose, ranging from introductory material to advanced operational guidance.

today: RFC 1150 is historic and was replaced by RFC 6360. The FYI series continues as part of the RFC family.

sections.title: What is the FYI Series
sections.content:
RFC 1150 is the first FYI note, formally titled "FYI on FYI: Introduction to the FYI Notes". The FYI series is designed as a central repository of information about Internet topics that do not fit the normative specification role of most RFCs. FYI documents may cover why something was done a certain way, answers to commonly asked questions, tutorial material for beginners, or advanced operational guidance. The intended audience ranges from newcomers to the Internet to experienced practitioners tackling complex problems.

FYIs are submitted to the IETF User Services Working Group for review before reaching the RFC Editor. Anyone can write an FYI if they have something to contribute and the time to do it.
sections.plainLanguage: FYIs are like a help desk. They answer "how do I..." and "why was..." questions. Anyone can write one.

sections.title: Why Part of the RFC Series
sections.content: FYIs are published as part of the RFC series rather than as a separate document type. This choice was made for practical reasons: the RFC distribution mechanisms are already proven and in place, so anyone who can access an RFC can automatically access an FYI. The RFC maintenance infrastructure is already funded and established, making it sensible to maintain similar documents the same way. Finally, the RFC name carries credibility in the Internet community, and FYIs benefit from that same respect and recognition.
sections.plainLanguage: Putting FYIs in the RFC library means everyone already knows where to find them, and the post office that delivers RFCs already handles them.

sections.title: Format and Distribution
sections.content:
FYIs must follow RFC format rules as specified in RFC 1111 (Requirements for RFC Authors). Each FYI must include a "Status of this Memo" section, a "Distribution Statement" (typically "unlimited"), a security considerations section, and an author's address section. Like all RFCs, FYIs are retrieved via FTP from NIC.DDN.MIL using the naming pattern FYI:mm.TXT (where mm is the FYI number), or through automated mail services.

The FYI series occasionally updates or obsoletes previous FYIs using the same UPDATES and OBSOLETES terminology as RFCs. A document that obsoletes an earlier FYI is complete on its own, while one that updates an FYI merely supplements the earlier document.
sections.plainLanguage: FYIs follow the same rules as RFCs: they have headers, sections, and an author address. You get them the same way you get RFCs.
